title: Phase 4 · Release: Ship It Safely
html:
Goal: act on the gate report Stage 3 left behind: the candidate is blocked on K1 (tokens per session), so developer requests a waiver, release-ops approves it, signs the release and moves live; then drill a one-click rollback and release again. After that, hand the agent to business systems through the public API (/v1/...), guard high-risk actions such as unauthorized payouts with a Cedar policy on the Gateway, and finally (optional) try A/B experiments and canaries and see how they relate to the release gate.

Prerequisites

This chapter starts from the state Stage 3 · Evaluate ends in:

Object State
Workspace default Release mode gated (Roles)
lab-service-assistant On live / candidate endpoints; live = v2 (old version), candidate = v3 (its system prompt gained one sentence: cite the policy rule id, e.g. R-01, A-03, H-02, for return, change/refund and cancellation answers)
Release record developer ran the gate (regression + holdout) on v3; verdict BLOCKED: red line P1 passed, and the only missed threshold is K1 (1,098 tokens per session against a bound of 500); state Blocked, nobody has signed, blocked or waived it yet
unicorn-service-criteria v1 Published and signed by biz-owner; criteria P1, P2, K1, C1, Q1, S1, S2; S2 was calibrated as not aligned, so C1, Q1, S1, S2 are only observed
unicorn-service-golden dev / regression / holdout = 24 / 15 / 9, holdout sealed

Accounts used in this chapter:

Account What it does here Why this account
developer Requests a waiver, redeploys and runs the gate once more, uses the API key, (optional) runs the A/B experiment and the canary The builder: holds agents.deploy and eval.run, but not release.sign or waiver.approve
release-ops Approves the waiver, signs off, rolls back The operator: holds release.sign and waiver.approve, but not agents.deploy, so it cannot change a prompt and release it itself
admin Attaches a Policy Engine to the Gateway, writes Cedar policies, switches to ENFORCE Platform administrator: the Gateway launchpad-gw is shared by the whole workspace, so changing it affects every agent that uses it

Sign in as developer in a normal browser window and as release-ops in a private/incognito window (or a second browser profile), so the two can take turns without signing out.

Chapter route

Part Content Accounts Required / optional Time
1 Gated release: blocked on K1 → request and approve a waiver → sign → rollback drill → release again release-ops, developer Required 50 min (the gate run for the re-release took under 20 min in this run)
2 Separation of duties and waiver rules (server-enforced) — Read 5 min
3 How release requests (/v3/releases) relate to the release gate — Read 5 min
4 Public API: the API key and curl calls from your own terminal developer Required 15 min
5 Cedar policy on the Gateway: LOG_ONLY → ENFORCE admin Required 25 min
6 A/B experiment (configuration bundles) developer Optional, advanced 60+ min
7 Runtime canaries and why they conflict with the gate developer Optional, advanced 5 min to read; 45+ min hands-on 
flowchart LR
  R[gate report from Stage 3<br/>BLOCKED: K1] --> W[developer<br/>requests a K1 waiver]
  W --> A[release-ops<br/>approves it]
  A --> P[report recomputed: PASS<br/>K1 waived]
  P --> S[release-ops signs<br/>live = v3]
  S --> RB[rollback drill<br/>live = v2]
  RB --> RD[developer redeploys v4<br/>gate runs again]
  RD --> S2[release-ops signs again<br/>live = v4]

1. Gated release

1.1 Recap: where things stand (release-ops)

  1. Sign in to the console (ConsoleUrl/v3) as release-ops.
  2. Click Release gate at the top of the rail (/v3/gate) and pick lab-service-assistant in the agent drop-down at the top right of the page (the URL becomes /v3/gate?agent=<id>). The page reads the release state every time it opens; whenever this chapter says "refresh", reload the browser page (this page has no separate refresh button).

Expected result (measured in this run):

  • Page title Blocked — a standard was not met.
  • Four figures at the top: Live v2, footnote on the named live endpoint; Candidate v3, footnote Blocked; Verdict BLOCKED; Standard v1, footnote signed by biz-owner.
  • The four gates: Red lines passed, Denominator passed, Thresholds 1 threshold missed, Observed not reached.
  • In the Criteria table, K1 智能体单次咨询消耗不超过 500 token (tokens per consultation ≤ 500) reads below threshold; C1, Q1, S1 and S2 have tier Observed and read judge not calibrated — observed until calibrated. The Cost tile under Five dimensions shows 1,098 against <= 500. In the measured column P1 and P2 read 25,671 ms (against <= 60,000 and <= 30,000) and K1 reads 1,098 (<= 500).
  • The Criteria card offers Sign and release (disabled, tooltip Only a passing gate can be signed off.) and Block; Release history has one row: v3, Blocked, developer.

Two kinds of "version": the Release gate page shows AWS Runtime versions (what the live and candidate endpoints point to); the Version column in the Agents list (and the Version figure at the top of an agent's page) is the platform's publish count. They need not match. In this chapter "version" always means the AWS version on the Release gate page.

K1 is a threshold, not a red line, so this block can be released under a waiver. In Stage 3 biz-owner set the cost budget at 500 tokens per session, while the measured usage is a mean of 742 on regression and 1,098 on holdout. The business decides to ship at the current usage and have the developer optimize the prompt and retrieval within two weeks; that is the reason in the waiver below. How the other verdicts are handled is at the end of Part 2.

1.2 Request a waiver (developer)

The V3 Release gate page does not handle waivers; they live on the Release gate tab of the Standards page.

  1. As developer, expand Agent evaluation under Modules in the rail and click Standards (/v3/standards), pick lab-service-assistant in Choose an agent at the top right, and switch to the Release gate tab (the URL is /v3/standards?agent=<id>&view=release). The Candidate v3 card shows BLOCKED at its top right; below it the Waivers card reads No waiver. and offers Request a waiver at its top right.

  2. Click Request a waiver. The dialog Request a waiver starts with A red line cannot be waived. Only a threshold gate can. Fill it in:

    Field Value
    Key K1 — 智能体单次咨询消耗不超过 500 token (the only entry: the list offers blocked, non-red-line criteria only)
    Why ship anyway The 500 tokens/session budget is below current usage; the developer will optimize the prompt and retrieval within two weeks. Release at current usage for now.
    Risk owner biz-owner (a named person, not a team; the business owner set the cost budget)
    Expires in (days) 14 (default 7, at most 30)
    Compensating control Check tokens per session on the Observe page daily; redeploy and rerun the gate once optimized

  3. Click Request a waiver in the dialog.

In the image: 1 Key K1 (only blocked, non-red-line criteria are offered); 2 Why ship anyway; 3 Risk owner biz-owner, Expires in (days) 14; 4 Compensating control; 5 click Request a waiver.

Expected result: toast Waiver requested; the Waivers table gains a row: Key K1, Status Waiting, Risk owner biz-owner, Expires 14 days out (2026-10-24 in this run), Times waived 1. Measured / required reads 1,098 (<= 500): 1,098 tokens per session against a bound of 500. developer gets no Approve button on the row.

1.3 Approve the waiver (release-ops)

  1. As release-ops, open the same page (Standards → lab-service-assistant → Release gate tab); the waiver row now offers Approve / Reject.
  2. Click Approve. The dialog Approve this waiver lists Key K1, Why ship anyway, Risk owner biz-owner, Compensating control and Expires 2026-10-24; check them and click Approve.

In the image: 1 check Key K1, Why ship anyway, Risk owner biz-owner, Compensating control, Expires 2026-10-24; 2 click Approve.

Expected result:

  • Toast Waiver approved; the waiver Status becomes Approved and the row ends with Revoke.
  • On the same tab the Candidate v3 card changes from BLOCKED to PASS, and in History the v3 decision changes from Blocked to Waiting for a signature. No gate re-run is needed: the report is recomputed with the waivers currently in force.
  • Back on the Release gate page (rail Release gate, or the candidate card's Open the release gate): title Cleared all four gates, Candidate footnote Waiting for a signature, Verdict PASS; in The four gates Thresholds reads passed and Observed 4 recorded; the K1 row no longer reads below threshold.

1.4 Sign and release (release-ops)

  1. Click Sign and release at the top right of the Criteria card. The dialog Sign and release says "The live endpoint is re-pointed to the candidate, so traffic moves the moment you confirm." and shows Verdict PASS, Waived K1, Live after this v3 and Rollback target v2.
  2. Write the reason in Note (optional when signing, required when blocking or rolling back): K1 is covered by the approved waiver; red line and denominator pass. Approved to go live, and click Sign and release in the dialog.

In the image: 1 Verdict PASS, Waived K1, Live after this v3, Rollback target v2; 2 write the reason in Note; 3 click Sign and release.

Expected result:

  • Toast Released — live moved to the candidate; the page title becomes Nothing waiting on the gate, Live v3 (on the named live endpoint), Candidate reads nothing pending.
  • In Release history that row becomes v3, Released, release-ops. The record also stores the id of the waiver it used (waiver_ids), so the report stays traceable.

1.5 Rollback drill (release-ops)

Suppose that after release a partner channel complains about how the rule ids are displayed and the change must be undone immediately.

  1. In the Release history card at the bottom of the Release gate page, click Roll back (top right of the card).
  2. The dialog Roll back says "The live endpoint is re-pointed to the previous version. Nothing is deleted." Fill in Note (required): Rollback drill: channel display issue, and click Roll back in the dialog.

Expected result:

  • Toast Rolled back; Live is back at v2 and the title still reads Nothing waiting on the gate.
  • Release history reads v2 Rolled back (the row the rollback added, decided by release-ops), then v3 Rolled back (the row that was Released).
  • A rollback only re-points live to v2; it deletes no version and rebuilds nothing: v3 and the candidate endpoint are still there (in step 1 of 1.6, Versions and endpoints lists v1–v4 as READY).

1.6 Release again (developer → release-ops)

A rollback cannot be "undone": the v3 record is now Rolled back and cannot be signed again, and another Roll back finds no Released record and returns release.nothing_to_roll_back (backend/app/dlc/releases.py). To bring the new prompt back to live, go through the gate once more:

  1. developer clicks Agents in the rail → lab-service-assistant, then Manage at the top right of the agent page, which opens the agent management page (a V2 page shown inside the V3 shell). Click Edit, leave the system prompt unchanged (the Stage 3 rule-id sentence is still there), click Next, and on the Review and deploy step click Save and redeploy. Every redeploy creates a new version on the same Runtime, v4 in this run, deployed in 27 seconds: once it finishes, Versions and endpoints shows DEFAULT 4, candidate 4, live 2.
  2. Click Release gate in the rail: title A candidate is waiting, Candidate v4, footnote Waiting for a signature; Release history gains v4 Waiting for a signature (developer). The gate's evaluation runs invoke the candidate endpoint themselves, so no warm-up is needed.
  3. developer checks Estimated cost in the Run the gate card (both splits' items × 1 repeat, judge cost included; it matches the sum of the two k = 1 split estimates in section 10 of the Evaluate chapter) and clicks Run the gate (this page always runs with one repeat; to change Repeats (k), run it from the Standards → Release gate tab instead). The page shows The gate runs are in progress… and the Candidate footnote reads Evaluating. In this run, once both runs (release 4 · regression, release 4 · holdout) showed Completed in Evaluation tasks (/v3/tasks), a reload of the Release gate page gave the verdict PASS: K1 measured 1,060 this time (still above 500), but the waiver approved in 1.3 has not expired, so it is counted under Waived again; the P95 for P1 / P2 was 17,212 ms. In this run, on the first reload after completion the verdict was already PASS but the Candidate footnote and the Release history row still read Evaluating; one more reload showed Waiting for a signature.
  4. release-ops signs as in 1.4: the dialog shows Verdict PASS, Waived K1, Live after this v4, Rollback target v2; enter v4 has the same prompt as v3 and K1 is still under its waiver; approved to release again in Note and click Sign and release; toast Released — live moved to the candidate.

Expected result:

  • Live v4; Release history reads v4 Released, v2 Rolled back, v3 Rolled back, all decided by release-ops.
  • On the agent page (rail Agents → lab-service-assistant): Lifecycle shows Candidate v4, Gate clear, Serving v4; in the Versions card the Serving on column of v4 lists DEFAULT, candidate and live.

In the image: 1 title Nothing waiting on the gate; 2 Live v4, on the named live endpoint; 3 Release history: v4 Released, v2 Rolled back (the row the rollback added), v3 Rolled back; 4 the Roll back button.

If you are short of time and skip 1.6, live stays on v2 while the agent's ledger stores the new system prompt. The production traffic seen in Stage 5 · Observe and the answers in Stage 6 · Feed back then come from v2. That does not change any step in those chapters.

2. Separation of duties and waiver rules

Every step in Part 1 is checked by "another person", and the server enforces it, not just by hiding buttons. This run verified the first two rules; the rest come from backend/app/dlc/releases.py and backend/app/core/route_policy.py:

Rule When violated
Only holders of release.sign can sign In this run developer calling POST /api/agents/{id}/release/sign got 403 auth.permission_required (This action requires the 'release.sign' permission); developer also sees neither Sign and release nor Block on the Release gate page
Only holders of waiver.approve can approve, reject or revoke a waiver In this run developer calling POST /api/waivers/{id}/approve got 403 auth.permission_required ('waiver.approve' permission); requesting a waiver only takes workspace membership
The signer ≠ the requester of the release record (whoever redeployed), administrators included 409 release.self_sign
The approver ≠ the waiver requester 409 waiver.self_approve
No signing without a PASS verdict 409 release.gate_not_passed
Red lines are never waived (the Request a waiver list does not offer them either) 409 waiver.redline
A reason and a risk owner are required waiver.incomplete
Expiry in the future and at most 30 days away waiver.bad_expiry / waiver.too_long

A waiver covers "this criterion on this agent" and is not tied to one release record: while it has not expired, every later gate report counts it under Waived (as the v4 report in 1.6 did). That is why release-ops can click Revoke in the Waivers table and confirm to end it at once (the confirmation says "The waiver on K1 stops covering the gate immediately; the next gate run treats that criterion as blocked again."). A second waiver on the same criterion shows 2× waived under Times waived, with the warning "A criterion waived more than once is a standard problem, not an exception. Change the threshold or fix the agent."

The other verdicts did not occur in this run; backend/app/dlc/gate.py decides them: on PASS, sign as in 1.4 directly; when the gate stops at Red lines (the row reads … violation(s) — red lines are never waived), release-ops clicks Block and fills in the required Note, and developer fixes, redeploys as in 1.6 and runs the gate again; INVALID (stopped at Denominator) cannot be waived: fix the evidence, then redeploy to open a new record.

3. How release requests relate to the release gate

Modules → Agent runtime → Releases in the rail (/v3/releases, page title Releases) and the Release card on the agent management page (opened with Manage on an agent's page) handle a different hand-off:

Release gate (Part 1) Release requests (/v3/releases)
Scope Inside one workspace: candidate → live Across workspaces, e.g. dev → prod
What is frozen Candidate version + criteria version + golden versions at that moment A release bundle: spec, artifact coordinates, evaluation evidence and policy posture, reduced to one digest
Who approves A holder of release.sign, ≠ requester A holder of promotion.approve, ≠ requester (app/services/promotion.py, administrators included)
Checks before execution The four gates Evaluation score, artifact, target workspace ready, deploy window; a prod-tier target also requires its Gateway Policy Engine in ENFORCE

Where they meet: a deploy driven by a release request moves live in the target workspace directly and does not open a release record, because the approved request is that decision.

This workshop has only one workspace, default, so the Release card on the agent management page says "No other workspace is registered, so there is nowhere to release to yet." and All requests on /v3/releases is empty. That is expected; there is no hands-on promotion in this chapter. The Release gate button at the top right of /v3/releases takes you back to the Release gate page from Part 1. Switching the Gateway to ENFORCE in Part 5 is exactly one of the conditions a future release into a prod workspace would have to meet.

4. Public API: hand the agent to business systems

Unicorn Mall's order system and Unicorn Trip's itinerary service will never sign in to the console; they call the agent through the public API (/v1/...). The public API runs the same invoke chain as console chat (the same invoke entry point), only authenticated with an X-Api-Key header; for an agent on named endpoints it also calls live only.

Route Purpose
GET /v1/agents List the active agents this key can see
POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/invoke Synchronous call
POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/invoke-stream Streaming call (SSE)

4.1 Issue an API key (developer)

  1. The V3 Chat page has no API key panel; keys are issued on the full chat page. As developer, open ConsoleUrl/v2/chat?full=1 in the address bar: this is the V2 Chat Playground, still shown inside the V3 shell (full=1 keeps the console on this page instead of handing over to V3 Chat).
  2. In the right panel switch to the API tab and click New key in the API keys section. Keys belong to the workspace, so it does not matter which agent the page has selected.
  3. The full key (lp_live_ followed by 32 hex characters) appears once with the note copy now — shown once. Copy it right away.

Expected result: under New key a green notice copy now — shown once shows the full key (with Copy next to it); a new row console-1 shows only the key prefix (lp_live_8a18… in this run), status Enabled, with Disable at the end of the row; the line under the prefix reads Created by developer · never used (after the first call, last used <time>). After a page reload the green notice is gone. The ledger keeps only the key's sha256 digest; a lost key can only be replaced.

In the image: 1 the API tab; 2 New key; 3 the new key console-1, prefix only, with its creator developer and last use on the line below, Enabled, with Disable at the end of the row.

Do not switch agents or send messages on this page: either rewrites the URL without full=1, and the console takes you back to V3 Chat. To come back, open ConsoleUrl/v2/chat?full=1 again.

An API key belongs to the current workspace: this key can call every active agent in workspace default. It also records its creator and lapses with the creator's account: when that account is deleted, disabled, expires or loses its grant to the workspace, the key is disabled automatically, /v1 returns 401, and it cannot be re-enabled (creator_offboarded in backend/app/services/api_keys.py). The seeded developer never expires; a key minted by a self-registered account (valid for 7 days) lapses when that account expires. The backend supports scoping by agent, expiry and rate limit (agent_ids, expires_at, rate_per_minute on POST /api/apikeys), but the console (V3 has no key page of its own and uses the full chat page above) currently only creates keys by name and enables or disables them. Do not capture the plaintext key in screenshots or recordings.

Also note the agent ID: click Agents in the rail → lab-service-assistant; the value after id= in the page URL /v3/agents?id=<id> is the ID (the line above the page title shows only its first 8 characters). On the agent management page opened with Manage, the ID row of the Basic information card is the same, and the Integration card generates curl / Python / JavaScript snippets.

4.2 Set up variables in your own terminal

This section runs in a terminal on your own computer: Terminal on macOS, any terminal on Linux, PowerShell on Windows (the commands are in the expandable block at the end of this section). It needs only curl — no jq, no AWS credentials, no AWS CLI: the API key issued in the previous step is the authentication. Anyone without a terminal can follow along with a teammate who has one; for the part you can see without a terminal, section 4.5 shows the browser way.

macOS / Linux (bash or zsh):

bash
export CONSOLE_URL='https://dxxxxxxxxxxxx.cloudfront.net'   # your team's ConsoleUrl from the organiser, no trailing /
export AGENT_ID='<ID of lab-service-assistant>'
read -rs LP_KEY && export LP_KEY                            # paste the API key and press Enter; nothing is echoed
curl -s "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents" -H "X-Api-Key: $LP_KEY"; echo

Reading the key with read -rs keeps it off the screen and out of the shell history; every later command only says $LP_KEY.

Expected result: one line of JSON (1,477 bytes in this run, with no trailing newline, which is why the command ends with ; echo) starting {"agents":[{"id":"<AGENT_ID>","name":"lab-service-assistant","display_name":null,"method":"zip_runtime","version":"4","attachment_capability":{..., one entry per active agent: lab-service-assistant (zip_runtime, "version":"4"), lab-policy-advisor (harness, "version":"2") and lab-legacy-agent (byoc, "version":"1"). Every entry also carries an attachment_capability block (the attachment types it accepts), so the line is long; the terminal's find (⌘F / Ctrl+Shift+F) on lab-service-assistant is the quickest way in. version is the platform ledger's publish count, not the AWS version behind live. The request path is CloudFront → nginx (which proxies /v1/) → backend.

Windows (PowerShell): every command of this section

Windows 10 / 11 ship curl.exe. In PowerShell always type curl.exe: in Windows PowerShell 5.1, curl is an alias of Invoke-WebRequest, with entirely different parameters. Put the Chinese questions into UTF-8 files and send them with -d "@file", so PowerShell does not mangle the quotes inside the JSON.

powershell
[Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.Encoding]::UTF8          # show Chinese answers correctly
$CONSOLE_URL = 'https://dxxxxxxxxxxxx.cloudfront.net'       # your team's ConsoleUrl from the organiser, no trailing /
$AGENT_ID = '<ID of lab-service-assistant>'
$LP_KEY = [Net.NetworkCredential]::new('', (Read-Host 'API key' -AsSecureString)).Password   # nothing is echoed

# 4.2 list agents
curl.exe -s "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents" -H "X-Api-Key: $LP_KEY"

# 4.3 synchronous call
[IO.File]::WriteAllText("$PWD\ask.json", '{"prompt":"我订了独角兽航空 UC1234 的经济舱特价票，明天出发，现在改签要收多少钱？"}')
curl.exe -s -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke" -H "X-Api-Key: $LP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "@ask.json"

# 4.4 streaming call
[IO.File]::WriteAllText("$PWD\ask-stream.json", '{"prompt":"独角兽酒店的提前预付价，入住前一天取消能退多少？两句话回答。"}')
curl.exe -sN -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke-stream" -H "X-Api-Key: $LP_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "@ask-stream.json"

# 4.5 wrong key, missing key header
[IO.File]::WriteAllText("$PWD\hi.json", '{"prompt":"hi"}')
curl.exe -s -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke" -H "X-Api-Key: lp_live_wrong" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "@hi.json" -w "`nHTTP %{http_code}`n"
curl.exe -s -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "@hi.json" -w "`nHTTP %{http_code}`n"

The expected results are the same as in the subsections below. [IO.File]::WriteAllText writes UTF-8 without a BOM; do not swap in Windows PowerShell 5.1's Set-Content -Encoding utf8, which writes a BOM at the start of the file.

4.3 Synchronous call

bash
curl -s -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $LP_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"我订了独角兽航空 UC1234 的经济舱特价票，明天出发，现在改签要收多少钱？"}'; echo

(The prompt asks: "I booked a Unicorn Air UC1234 economy saver fare departing tomorrow; how much does a change cost now?")

Expected result: one line of JSON (no indentation) with these fields (laid out on several lines here for reading):

json
{
    "agent": "lab-service-assistant",
    "text": "<answer based on the change/refund policy>",
    "session_id": "<server-generated 64-hex-character session id>",
    "latency_ms": 12597,
    "answered_by": "model"
}
  • One observed answer (v4, latency_ms 12597) first explains the three economy fare brands 轻享 / 标准 / 灵活 (Light / Standard / Flex, A-01) and treats a "saver" fare as Light; departing tomorrow falls in window W2, so the change fee is 40% of the base fare (A-02), at least ¥50 (A-04), plus any fare difference (A-05); it then warns that a Light fare cannot be changed within 4 hours of departure and that an airline-caused disruption allows a free change (A-08), and ends by asking for the fare brand and base fare.
  • The answer comes from the version live currently points to (v4 after Part 1): the public API sees the same version as console chat.
  • The body is one unindented line with no trailing newline (the ; echo at the end of the command adds one); Chinese text comes out as is, not escaped as \uXXXX; line breaks inside text show as \n. No jq is needed; if you format it with another tool, avoid python3 -m json.tool, which escapes Chinese as \uXXXX.
  • Multi-turn: send the returned session_id back unchanged in the next request body's "session_id" field.
  • Content-Type: application/json is required, otherwise you get 422 validation.invalid_request.

4.4 Streaming call (SSE)

bash
curl -sN -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke-stream" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $LP_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"独角兽酒店的提前预付价，入住前一天取消能退多少？两句话回答。"}'

(The prompt asks, in two sentences, how much of a Unicorn Hotels prepaid advance-purchase rate is refunded when cancelling the day before check-in.)

Expected result: meta first; this question searches the knowledge base first, so a tool event follows; then many delta events (84 in this run, one or two words each), then done; no : keep-alive line appeared in this run:

text
event: meta
data: {"session_id": "<SESSION_ID>", "agent": "lab-service-assistant", "mode": "stream"}

event: tool
data: {"name": "kb_search", "id": "call_0"}

event: delta
data: {"text": "<incremental text>"}

event: done
data: {"latency_ms": 9372}

One observed answer (the 84 delta texts joined): "您好，独角兽酒店没有“提前预付价”，您说的应该是标准预付价：按 H-03 条款，入住时间前不足 48 小时取消，将收取首晚房费，其余房费退还。入住前一天取消已不足 48 小时，因此可退还除首晚外的其余房费（若只订一晚则无退款）。" (Unicorn Hotels has no "advance-purchase" rate, so it reads it as the standard prepaid rate: under H-03 a cancellation less than 48 hours before check-in costs the first night and the rest is refunded; the day before is inside 48 hours, so everything but the first night comes back, and a one-night booking gets nothing back.)

Event Meaning
meta Session id, agent name, mode (stream for Strands ZIP: native model increments)
delta Incremental text
tool A tool call (e.g. knowledge base retrieval), depending on the question
rule A curated answer rule matched
done Finished, with end-to-end latency
error Failure, with code / message

The stream may also contain : keep-alive comment lines that keep the connection open. CloudFront's origin read timeout is 60 seconds; prefer the streaming route for long answers, since a synchronous call that takes longer than 60 seconds can get a 504.

4.5 What an authentication failure looks like

bash
# wrong key
curl -s -X POST "$CONSOLE_URL/v1/agents/$AGENT_ID/invoke" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: lp_live_wrong" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n'

# no key header

5. Cedar policy on the Gateway: from LOG_ONLY to ENFORCE

5.1 What this protects in the scenario

The release gate answers "may this version ship"; a Cedar policy answers "which tool actions may the shipped agent call". What Unicorn Company fears most is an agent issuing a refund, a ticket or a price change nobody authorized. Even if the prompt says "do not overstep", the last line of defence belongs in the tool layer: an unauthorized caller should simply not be able to invoke those actions.

In this deployment the Governance list has two Gateways: launchpad-kb-gw is created by the platform for managed knowledge base retrieval (lab-unicorn-policies sits on it) and is left alone here; the platform's own Gateway launchpad-gw carries two demo targets (the base stack's Lambda launchpad-hr-database and an OpenAPI target office-facts); there is no real refund or ticketing tool. We use the only "money-moving" action among them to demonstrate the same pattern:

Action on launchpad-gw Nature Unicorn Company tool it stands for
hr-database___create_payout Finance write action (the demo Lambda only returns a simulated PAY-… record; no money moves, nothing is stored) Refund payouts, compensation, ticket issuance, price changes: actions with money or order consequences
hr-database___get_employee, hr-database___list_departments, hr-database___check_calendar Read-only lookups Order, stock, flight and hotel status lookups
office-facts___get_office_fact, office-facts___list_office_topics Read-only knowledge Rules and announcements

Target policy: every authenticated caller may use the read-only actions; the finance write action is only for identities in the platform-admin group. In production, register Unicorn's refund / ticketing / pricing APIs as Gateway targets and apply exactly the same two policies.

launchpad-gw is shared by every agent in the workspace. admin does this part, strictly in order: attach the engine in LOG_ONLY, write the policies, collect evidence, promote the policies to ACTIVE, and only then switch the Gateway to ENFORCE. ENFORCE is default-deny: without an ACTIVE permit, every agent using this Gateway loses all of its tools. In this workshop lab-service-assistant and lab-policy-advisor retrieve policies through the knowledge base connector and do not depend on these two demo targets, so their answers are not affected.

5.3 Write two LOG_ONLY policies (admin)

Policy 1: tool allowlist

  1. Open the Policies section, click New policy; the page NEW LOG_ONLY POLICY opens.

    cedar
    permit(
  principal is AgentCore::OAuthUser,
  action in [AgentCore::Action::"hr-database___get_employee", ...],
  resource == AgentCore::Gateway::"arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-east-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:gateway/<GATEWAY_ID>"
);

  2. AUTHORIZATION MODEL: Custom Cedar; paste into the Cedar box (replace the Gateway ARN):

    cedar
    forbid(
  principal is AgentCore::OAuthUser,
  action == AgentCore::Action::"hr-database___create_payout",
  resource == AgentCore::Gateway::"<Gateway ARN copied above>"
) unless {
  principal.hasTag("cognito:groups") &&
  principal.getTag("cognito:groups") like "*platform-admin*"
};

  3. Click Create LOG_ONLY policy and click Confirm in the Save policy dialog.

Expected result: the Policies section lists both policies with Status ACTIVE (the AWS resource status) and Policy mode LOG_ONLY. In Cedar a forbid overrides a permit, so together they mean: read-only actions for everyone, create_payout only for the platform-admin group.

Policy names may contain only letters, digits and underscores and must start with a letter (no hyphens). You can also describe the intent in NATURAL-LANGUAGE GENERATION on the right (for example "forbid users outside the platform-admin group from calling hr-database___create_payout"), click Generate and bring the result in with Use this Cedar, but review it line by line before saving.

6. (Optional, advanced) A/B experiment: test a new prompt with configuration bundles

An A/B experiment answers "is the AI-recommended prompt really better than the current one". It switches prompts on the same Runtime with AgentCore configuration bundles, without a rebuild, so only Launchpad-managed HTTP runtimes such as Strands ZIP are supported. lab-service-assistant qualifies; the Harness-based lab-policy-advisor does not.

How it gets along with the gate (from backend/app/optimization/service.py):

  • Experiment traffic is a replay of dataset questions through a dedicated experiment gateway launchpad-exp-gw; it does not split real users. Real users keep going to live.
  • The experiment gateway target uses the DEFAULT endpoint (the Runtime's latest version); the two arms differ only in the prompt carried by their bundles.
  • Promote writes the treatment prompt back to the agent and runs the normal deploy pipeline. In a gated workspace that deploy, like the Stage 3 redeploy, lands on candidate only and opens a new release record: winning an A/B test does not bypass the gate. The gate still has to run and release-ops still signs before live moves.

Every stage is triggered by hand and saved immediately, so a page reload never loses progress. Only one experiment can run per workspace at a time.

7. (Optional, advanced) Runtime canaries: why not on a gated agent

A Runtime canary (A/B experiments, switched to Runtime canaries at the top right) moves an agent's real production traffic through a dedicated canary gateway to a candidate version in steps of 90/10 → 50/50 → 1/99, recording a verdict before each step, and ends with PROMOTE TO PRODUCTION or ROLL BACK. The banner says it plainly: "Promote and roll back really change what production serves."

It is built on the premise that "DEFAULT is production", while a gated agent's production is live. Nothing in the code (backend/app/optimization/canary_service.py, backend/app/services/invoke.py) checks for gated agents, so a canary on lab-service-assistant would cause three problems:

Problem Why
It bypasses the gate While a canary runs, every call is routed through the canary gateway instead of live
The control arm may be an unreleased version The control arm is the Runtime's latest version, which on a gated agent can be an unsigned candidate rather than what live serves
"Promote" never reaches production Promote only updates the platform ledger; it does not move live and opens no release record. After cleanup, calls go back to live, still on the old version

Conclusion: for an agent on live/candidate endpoints, the gradual rollout tool is the gate itself (evaluate on candidate, sign to move live, roll back at any time); do not add a canary on top. Canaries are for agents still on a Single endpoint (direct).

Run the gate is disabled with Over the workspace limit next to it (the API returns run.cost_over_limit) The estimate exceeds the workspace's refusal limit admin raises Refuse above (USD) in the Release policy card on the Standards → Release gate tab and clicks Save, or lower the repeats
Run the gate is disabled for developer The account lacks eval.run Run it as the developer account that holds eval.run
A gate run fails or times out waiting for telemetry Some sessions' telemetry had not landed before the run ended, or a model call hit a transient error Read the failure in the Evaluation tasks list, and a few minutes later click Run the gate again on the gate page
The report is INVALID and lists an unsigned standard biz-owner has not signed the current criteria version (the Standard figure reads not signed) Have biz-owner sign, then reload the Release gate page
Signing returns release.self_sign The signer is the requester of this deploy Have another holder of release.sign sign
Rolling back returns release.nothing_to_roll_back No record is currently Released (never signed, or already rolled back) Sign a release first; after a rollback, release again as in 1.6
Approving a waiver returns waiver.self_approve Approver and requester are the same account Let release-ops approve developer's request
A synchronous /v1 call returns 422 validation.invalid_request Content-Type: application/json is missing, or session_id is shorter than 33 characters Add the header; reuse the session_id the server returned
A synchronous /v1 call returns 504 The answer took longer than CloudFront's 60-second origin timeout Use invoke-stream
New policy is disabled The Gateway is not managed, has no Policy Engine, or a shared Policy Engine needs acknowledging Follow the button's hint
Apply Gateway mode is disabled The Gateway name is missing, the IAM preflight fails, or there is no evidence and no override reason Fix what the card lists above the button
After ENFORCE an agent has lost all its tools ENFORCE is default-deny and no ACTIVE permit covers those actions Switch the Gateway back to LOG_ONLY at once, add the permit, then switch again
Start experiment is disabled and the page says "An experiment is already running — …" The shared experiment gateway supports one A/B test at a time Clean up the previous experiment first
After working on ConsoleUrl/v2/chat?full=1 you land back on V3 Chat You switched agents or sent a message, which drops full=1 from the URL Open ConsoleUrl/v2/chat?full=1 again and only use the API tab
